## Why This Is Asked
This question evaluates the ability to design a practical multilingual NLP solution under real-time constraints with privacy considerations—skills essential for consumer-facing products at major tech companies.

This question evaluates end-to-end system design for multilingual, real-time sarcasm detection with code-switching support, drift control, weak supervision capabilities, and privacy-by-design principles.

## Key Concepts

- **Multilingual encoders and code-switching robustness**: Handling mixed-language input seamlessly
- **Streaming architectures and latency budgeting**: Processing messages in real-time with minimal delay
- **Per-language drift detection and calibration**: Monitoring and adjusting for distribution shifts in each supported language
- **Weak supervision labeling**: Leveraging heuristic or noisy labels to train models without exhaustive manual annotation
- **Privacy-by-design**: Minimizing data collection and ensuring user privacy throughout the pipeline
- **Safe rollback mechanisms**: Implementing safeguards to revert to previous model versions when performance degrades

## Why This Is Asked
This question probes real-time, multilingual NLP design under data scarcity with robust explainability and rollout safety.

## Key Concepts
- Streaming NLP with adapters
- Multilingual encoders (XLM-R), zero/few-shot adaptation
- Drift & fairness monitoring per language
- Token-level explainability over recent context
- Canary rollouts and automatic rollback

## Code Example
```javascript
// Example: simple adapter switch in inference path
function infer(message, lang, adapters){
  const base = encoder.encode(message, lang)
  const rep = adapters[lang]?.apply(base) ?? base
  return classifier.predict(rep)
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you evaluate fairness across languages?
- How to ensure explainability remains stable with new intents?

}
